readings.title: Barzillai the Gil‛aḏite
readings.subtitle: Dawiḏ Blesses an Old Friend
readings.text: [2 Samuel 19:31] And Barzillai the Gil‛aḏite came down from Rogelim and went across the Yardĕn with the sovereign, to send him on across <dn>את</dn> the Yardĕn. [32] Now Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old. And he had provided <dn>את</dn> the sovereign with food while he stayed at Maḥanayim, for he was a very great man. [33] And the sovereign said to Barzillai, “Come across with me, and I shall provide for <dn>את</dn> you with me in Yerushalayim.” [34] But Barzillai said to the sovereign, “How many days are the years of my life, that I should go up with the sovereign to Yerushalayim? [35] “I am eighty years old today. Do I know between good and evil? Does your servant taste <dn>את</dn> what I eat or <dn>את</dn> what I drink? Do I hear any longer <dn>את</dn> the voice of singing men and singing women? Why then should your servant be a further burden to my master the sovereign? [36] “Your servant goes a little way across the Yardĕn with the sovereign. And why should the sovereign repay me with such a reward? [37] “Please let your servant turn back, so that I die in my own city, near the grave of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham, let him cross over with <dn>את</dn> my master the sovereign, and do for him what is good in your eyes.” [38] And the sovereign answered, “Let Kimham cross over with me, and let me do for him <dn>את</dn> what is good in your eyes. And whatever you choose to ask of me, I do for you.” [39] And all the people went over the Yardĕn. And when the sovereign had crossed over, the sovereign kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place. [40] And the sovereign went on to Gilgal, and Kimham went on with him. And all the people of Yehuḏah, and also half the people of Yisra’ĕl, brought <dn>את</dn> the sovereign across.

readings.title: A Dispute Over the Sovereign
readings.subtitle: Yisra’ĕl and Yehuḏah Clash
readings.text: [2 Samuel 19:41] And see, all the men of Yisra’ĕl came to the sovereign, and said to the sovereign, “Why have our brothers, the men of Yehuḏah, stolen you away and brought <dn>את</dn> the sovereign, <dn>את</dn> his household, and all Dawiḏ’s men with him across the Yardĕn?” [42] And all the men of Yehuḏah answered the men of Yisra’ĕl, “Because the sovereign is a close relative of ours. Why then are you wroth over this matter? Have we eaten at all at the sovereign’s expense? Or has he given us any gift?” [43] And the men of Yisra’ĕl answered the men of Yehuḏah, and said, “We have ten parts in the sovereign, so we also have more right to Dawiḏ than you. Why then did you despise us – were we not the first to advise bringing back <dn>את</dn> our sovereign?” But the words of the men of Yehuḏah were harsher than the words of the men of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: The Rebellion of Sheḇa
readings.subtitle: Yo'aḇ's Ruthless Pursuit
readings.text: [2 Samuel 20:1] And a man of Beliya‛al was found there, whose name was Sheḇa son of Biḵri, a Binyaminite. And he blew a ram’s horn, and said, “We have no part in Dawiḏ, nor do we have inheritance in the son of Yishai! Every man to his tents, O Yisra’ĕl!” [2] So every man of Yisra’ĕl withdrew from Dawiḏ, and followed Sheḇa son of Biḵri. But the men of Yehuḏah, from the Yardĕn as far as Yerushalayim, clung to their sovereign. [3] And Dawiḏ came to his house at Yerushalayim. And the sovereign took <dn>את</dn> the ten women, his concubines whom he had left to guard the house, and put them in a house under guard, and provided for them, but did not go in to them. And they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood. [4] And the sovereign said to Amasa, “Call <dn>את</dn> the men of Yehuḏah to me within three days, and you be present here.” [5] So Amasa went to call <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah, but he delayed longer than the appointed time which Dawiḏ had appointed him. [6] And Dawiḏ said to Aḇishai, “Now Sheḇa son of Biḵri is going to do us more evil than Aḇshalom. Take <dn>את</dn> your master’s servants and pursue him, lest he find for himself walled cities, and snatch away our eyes.” [7] So Yo’aḇ’s men, with the Kerĕthites, and the Pelĕthites, and all the mighty men, went out after him. And they went out of Yerushalayim to pursue Sheḇa son of Biḵri. [8] When they were at the large stone which is in Giḇ‛on, Amasa came before them. Now Yo’aḇ was dressed in battle armour, and on it was a belt with a sword fastened in its sheath at his hips, and as he went forward it fell out. [9] And Yo’aḇ said to Amasa, “Is it well with you, my brother?” And Yo’aḇ took Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him. [10] But Amasa did not guard against the sword that was in Yo’aḇ’s hand. So he smote him in the stomach with it, and poured his entrails to the ground, and did not smite him a second time, and he died. And Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai his brother pursued Sheḇa son of Biḵri. [11] And one of Yo’aḇ’s young men stood by him, and said, “Whoever delights in Yo’aḇ and whoever is for Dawiḏ, follow Yo’aḇ!” [12] And Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he moved <dn>את</dn> Amasa from the highway to the field and threw a garment over him, when he saw that everyone who came upon him halted. [13] When he was removed from the highway, all the people went on after Yo’aḇ to pursue Sheḇa son of Biḵri.

readings.title: A Wise Woman Intervenes
readings.subtitle: The End of Sheḇa's Revolt
readings.text: [2 Samuel 20:14] And he passed through all the tribes of Yisra’ĕl to Aḇĕl, and Bĕyth Ma‛aḵah, and all the Bĕrites. And they were gathered together and also went after him. [15] And they came and besieged him in Aḇĕl of Bĕyth Ma‛aḵah. And they threw up a siege mound against the city, and it stood by the rampart. And all the people who were with Yo’aḇ were battering the wall to throw it down. [16] And a wise woman cried out from the city, “Listen! Listen! Please say to Yo’aḇ, ‘Come nearby, so that I speak with you.’ ” [17] And when he had come near to her, the woman said, “Are you Yo’aḇ?” And he answered, “I am.” And she said to him, “Hear the words of your female servant.” And he answered, “I am hearing.” [18] And she spoke, saying, “They used to speak in former times, saying, ‘Let them rightly ask at Aḇĕl,’ and so they ended it. [19] “I am among the peaceable and true ones in Yisra’ĕl. You seek to destroy a city and a mother in Yisra’ĕl. Why would you swallow up the inheritance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [20] And Yo’aḇ answered and said, “Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy! [21] “The matter is not so. But a man from the mountains of Ephrayim, Sheḇa son of Biḵri by name, has lifted up his hand against the sovereign, against Dawiḏ. Give up <dn>את</dn> him alone, and I withdraw from the city.” And the woman said to Yo’aḇ, “See, his head is thrown to you over the wall.” [22] And the woman in her wisdom went to all the people. And they cut off <dn>את</dn> the head of Sheḇa son of Biḵri, and threw it out to Yo’aḇ. And he blew a ram’s horn, and they withdrew from the city, every man to his tent. And Yo’aḇ returned to the sovereign at Yerushalayim. [23] And Yo’aḇ was over all the army of Yisra’ĕl, and Benayah son of Yehoyaḏa was over the Kerĕthites and over the Pelĕthites, [24] and Aḏoram was over the compulsory labour, and Yehoshaphat son of Aḥiluḏ was recorder, [25] and Shewa was scribe, and Tsaḏoq and Eḇyathar were priests, [26] and also Ira the Ya’irite was a chief ruler to Dawiḏ.

readings.title: The Guilt of Sha'ul's House
readings.subtitle: A Three-Year Famine
readings.text: [2 Samuel 21:1] And there was a scarcity of food in the days of Dawiḏ for three years, year after year. And Dawiḏ sought <dn>את</dn> the face of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered, <dq>“It is for Sha’ul and his bloodthirsty house, because he killed <dn>את</dn> the Giḇ‛onites.”</dq> [2] And the sovereign called the Giḇ‛onites and spoke to them. Now the Giḇ‛onites were not of the children of Yisra’ĕl, but of the remnant of the Amorites, and the children of Yisra’ĕl had sworn to them, but Sha’ul sought to smite them in his zeal for the children of Yisra’ĕl and Yehuḏah. [3] And Dawiḏ said to the Giḇ‛onites, “What do I do for you? And with what do I make atonement, that you might bless <dn>את</dn> the inheritance of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [4] And the Giḇ‛onites said to him, “We have no matter of silver or gold with Sha’ul or his house, nor is it for us to put anyone to death in Yisra’ĕl.” And he said, “Whatever you say, I do for you.” [5] And they said to the sovereign, “The man who consumed us and plotted against us, that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the borders of Yisra’ĕl, [6] let seven men of his sons be given to us, and we shall hang them before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Giḇ‛ah of Sha’ul, whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chose.” And the sovereign said, “I give them.” [7] But the sovereign spared Mephiḇosheth son of Yehonathan, son of Sha’ul, because of the oath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that was between them, between Dawiḏ and Yehonathan son of Sha’ul. [8] So the sovereign took <dn>את</dn> the two sons of Ritspah daughter of Ayah, whom she bore to Sha’ul: Armoni and Mephiḇosheth, and <dn>את</dn> the five sons of Miḵal daughter of Sha’ul, whom she brought up for Aḏri’ĕl son of Barzillai the Meholathite, [9] and gave them into the hands of the Giḇ‛onites, and they hung them on the hill before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. So the seven fell together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest. [10] And Ritspah daughter of Ayah took <dn>את</dn> sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until the late rains poured on them from the heavens. And she did not allow the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night. [11] And it was reported to Dawiḏ what Ritspah daughter of Ayah, the concubine of Sha’ul, had done. [12] And Dawiḏ went and took <dn>את</dn> the bones of Sha’ul, and <dn>את</dn> the bones of Yehonathan his son, from the men of Yaḇĕsh Gil‛aḏ who had stolen <dn>את</dn> them from the square of Bĕyth Shan, where the Philistines had hung <dn>את</dn> them up, the day the Philistines smote <dn>את</dn> Sha’ul in Gilboa. [13] And he brought up <dn>את</dn> the bones of Sha’ul and <dn>את</dn> the bones of Yehonathan his son from there. And they gathered <dn>את</dn> the bones of those who had been hung. [14] And they buried <dn>את</dn> the bones of Sha’ul and Yehonathan his son in the country of Binyamin in Tsĕla, in the tomb of Qish his father, and did all that the sovereign commanded. And after that <dn>Elohim</dn> was entreated for the land.

readings.title: Battles Against the Giants
readings.subtitle: Dawiḏ's Mighty Men
readings.text: [2 Samuel 21:15] And there was battle again between the Philistines and Yisra’ĕl. And Dawiḏ and his servants with him went down and fought against the Philistines, and Dawiḏ was tired. [16] And Yishbi-Bĕnoḇ, who was one of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose bronze spear was three hundred sheqels, who was bearing a new sword, thought he could smite <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ. [17] But Aḇishai son of Tseruyah came to his help, and smote <dn>את</dn> the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of Dawiḏ swore to him, saying, “You do not go out with us to battle anymore, lest you put out the lamp of Yisra’ĕl.” [18] And it came to be afterward that there was another battle with the Philistines at Goḇ. Then Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite smote <dn>את</dn> Saph, who was one of the sons of the giant. [19] And there was another battle in Goḇ with the Philistines, where Elḥanan son of Ya‛arĕy-Oreg̱im the Bĕyth Leḥemite smote <dn>את</dn> Golyath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam. [20] And there was another battle in Gath, where there was a man of great height, who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number. And he also was born to the giant. [21] And he reproached <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, and Yehonathan son of Shim‛i, Dawiḏ’s brother, smote him. [22] These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of Dawiḏ and by the hand of his servants. [1 Chronicles 20:4] And it came to be afterward, that a battle with the Philistines broke out at Gezer. Then Sibbeḵai the Ḥushathite smote <dn>את</dn> Sippai, who was one of the sons of the giant, and they were humbled. [5] And there was battle with the Philistines again, and Elḥanan son of Ya’ir smote <dn>את</dn> Laḥmi the brother of Golyath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam. [6] And there was battle in Gath again, where there was a man of great height, with twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand and six on each foot. And he also was born to the giant. [7] And he reproached <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ĕl, and Yehonathan son of Shim‛a, Dawiḏ’s brother, smote him. [8] These were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of Dawiḏ and by the hand of his servants.

readings.title: Save Me from All Those Who Pursue Me
readings.subtitle: A Shiggaion of Dawiḏ
readings.text: [Psalm 7:1] A Shiggaion of Dawiḏ, which he sang to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the words of Kush, a Binyaminite. O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, in <dn>You</dn> I have taken refuge; save me from all those who pursue me, and deliver me, [2] lest they tear me like a lion, ripping in pieces, with no one to deliver. [3] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, if I have done this: if there is unrighteousness in my hands, [4] if I have rewarded evil to him who was at peace with me, or have plundered my enemy without cause, [5] let the enemy pursue me and overtake my life, and trample my life to the earth, and lay my esteem in the dust. Selah. [6] Arise, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in <dn>Your</dn> displeasure; lift <dn>Yourself</dn> up against the rage of my enemies, and awake for me! <dn>You</dn> shall command right-ruling! [7] And let the congregation of the peoples gather about <dn>You</dn>; and over them return on high. [8] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> judges the peoples; rightly rule me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to my righteousness, and according to my integrity within me. [9] Please let the evil of the wrong be ended, and establish the righteous; for the righteous <dn>Elohim</dn> is a searcher of hearts and kidneys. [10] My shield is upon <dn>Elohim</dn>, who saves the upright in heart. [11] <dn>Elohim</dn> is a righteous judge, and <dn>Ěl</dn> is enraged every day. [12] If one does not repent, <dn>He</dn> sharpens <dn>His</dn> sword; <dn>He</dn> bends <dn>His</dn> bow and makes it ready, [13] and <dn>He</dn> prepares for <dn>Himself</dn> instruments of death; <dn>He</dn> makes <dn>His</dn> arrows hot for pursuers. [14] See, he is in labour with wickedness, and shall conceive trouble, and bring forth falsehood. [15] He has dug a pit and made it deep, and falls into the ditch he made. [16] His trouble returns upon his own head, and his violence comes down on the top of his head. [17] I give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> according to <dn>His</dn> righteousness, and praise the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH Most High</dn>.
